1.pericope_label: The beast rising out of the sea

debates.q: Who stood upon the sand?

sides.a: The dragon: so the versions and the Alexandrian copy, and the connection requires it
The dragon, halted on his way to war with the rest of her seed
The seer himself, as it seemed to him, though still in a rapture

debates.q: What power is the beast?

sides.a: The Roman Empire, whose emperors took blasphemous divine titles
The secular Roman power that upheld the church of Rome
The Roman papacy, a mixed power, prince and false prophet at once
The kingdom of the time of Antichrist, gathered from many nations
The body of the devil, springing from the people of the ungodly

outliers: Adam Clarke insists that the symbol be fixed from Scripture first, taking the angel’s own explanation of Daniel’s fourth beast as decisive that a beast is a kingdom

debates.q: Why does the beast combine three animals?

sides.a: Rome was in fact made up of the empires Daniel figured separately
It represents every form of world-power swift to shed blood
The leopard points to the Greek empire, which the Latin resembled

debates.q: What is the head wounded to death?

sides.a: The most perplexing question in the book; the heads are both hills and dynasties
The imperial power, ended in the west and healed by a new line of emperors
The death of Nero, with the pretenders after him and Domitian as Nero again
The blow struck at the Cross, whose fruits are delayed rather than lost

outliers: Charles Ellicott compares the three beasts of the vision to those that hindered the poet from ascending the pleasant mount

4.pericope_label: The world worships the dragon and the beast; blasphemies for forty-two months

debates.q: Is the homage paid to the dragon actual worship?

sides.view: Reverence to a superior power, not open adoration of Satan as God, though in effect his
Literal devil-worship; the beast is only the tool by which Satan receives it
The voluntary religious subjection of a church to the empire that protects it
Worship offered to the devil in the images, angels and departed saints

debates.q: What are the forty and two months?

sides.view: Prophetic days, so twelve hundred and sixty years, with the starting point unknown
The familiar symbolic period, simply the limited time of the world-power
A question of the verb: working signs for that duration, or merely doing time

outliers.view: Turns the beast-worship on the present, calling modern self-worship the same idolatry and naming might-makes-right as its creed

7.pericope_label: War on the saints, universal worship, and the Lamb’s book of life

debates.q: In what sense does the beast overcome the saints?

sides.view: Literally and historically, in wars and inquisitions that killed them by the hundred thousand
Not a conquest of their fidelity; only that they must suffer or submit
A textual point first — the clause is missing from good witnesses — and then simply that no one escaped the beast’s rule

debates.q: Does from the foundation of the world attach to slain or to written?

sides.view: To slain, as the common version has it, though the other construction makes sense
Both are possible; the simple order favours slain, and either way the security of the saints rests on eternal love
To slain, but of the foundation of the Christian world, dated from the crucifixion

outliers.view: Shrinks every universal in the passage to the Latin west — the earth, all kindreds and tongues, even the foundation of the world itself, mean the Christian empire and its beginning

9.pericope_label: The call to hear, and the law of retribution on captor and swordsman

debates.q: Is verse 10 a threat to the persecutor or a counsel to the persecuted?

sides.view: A law of retribution: the conquering power will suffer what it inflicted
A warning to the saints that the Church conquers by suffering, and that taking up the sword would be fatal to their success
Both — the first clause forbids Christians to resist force with force, the second draws the persecutor’s end

debates.q: What is the patience and faith of the saints?

sides.view: Keeping God’s retributive justice in view under persecution
Refusing world-like methods of self-rescue
Faithfulness rather than belief — submission to the inevitable

outliers.view: Sets aside the reading generally accepted in his day and makes the verse a caution against the saints arming themselves rather than a consolation about their fate

11.pericope_label: The second beast from the earth, lamb-horned and dragon-voiced

debates.q: What power is the second beast?

sides.view: The papacy in its spiritual and ecclesiastical character, the same antichrist in another light
The Romish hierarchy specifically, dated from its emancipation from the civil power
Not a historical body but world-power guided by earthly wisdom
The provincial power that imitated Rome in persecution — the Protestant reading falls outside the imagery

debates.q: Why does this beast rise from the earth and the first from the sea?

sides.view: Sea for the agitated conditions that bore the secular power, land for the settled ones that bore the spiritual
Sea for the passions of mankind, earth for consolidated human thought and culture
Earth means the Latin world, so the beast rises from subjection inside it
Perhaps to localise him in Asia Minor rather than give him world-wide scope

outliers.view: Names the Reformation reading of the two beasts, credits its plausibility, and then rejects it as outside what the imagery can bear

13.pericope_label: Lying wonders, the deception of the dwellers on earth, and the image of the beast

debates.q: Who can be deceived by the beast’s signs?

sides.view: Only the reprobate; the elect are secured against such deception
Whoever has lost the will to ask whether a thing is right
The public at large, whose gullibility Christ warned would reach even the elect if it could

debates.q: What is the image made to the beast?

sides.view: A coin, standard, bust or statue set up for the imperial cult
A person — the supreme ecclesiastical ruler of the Latin empire, not the emperor
The deified spirit of worldliness rather than any object

outliers.view: Argues the case from the newspapers of his own month, dating his page and citing a report of a picture of the Virgin whose eyes had moved

15.pericope_label: Breath given to the image, and death for refusing it worship

debates.q: What is the image that receives breath?

sides.view: The restored Roman civil power, vivified by an act of the Papacy
The pope himself — a private man until the clergy elect him and so give him life
A system working conjuring tricks, the speaking image being ventriloquism
No mechanism at all; wisdom lends a semblance of life to a doomed cause

debates.q: Is the homage demanded of the image civil or religious?

sides.view: Civil homage, allegiance to a jurisdiction on pain of death
Religious worship, which Christians died rather than render
A rite of adoration, robes, crowning and kissing of the feet

outliers.view: Opens the verse with a Hindu parallel, the consecration by incantation that gives a new idol eyes and a soul and with them a legal right to worship

16.pericope_label: The mark on hand and forehead, and the ban on buying and selling

debates.q: What is the mark of the beast?

sides.view: Latin worship — the mass and offices in Latin, the badge of one church against all others
A brand of ownership, like the master’s name on a slave
The imperial seal known from the papyri, stamped with the emperor’s name and image

debates.q: What is the ban on buying and selling?

sides.view: A first-century boycott of those who would not worship the emperor
Medieval interdict, documented from councils, synods and bulls against dissenters
A claim of jurisdiction over commerce, and so over the wealth of nations

outliers.view: Argues the mark from business papyri and branding practice rather than from church history, and treats name and number as one thing written two ways

18.pericope_label: Here is wisdom: the number of the beast

debates.q: What name yields six hundred and sixty-six?

sides.view: The Greek word for the Latin man, spelt with the diphthong
Not that word, whose spelling forbids it, but the Greek for the Latin kingdom
Perhaps Nero Caesar in Hebrew letters, which also explains the variant reading — but who can tell?
No name at all; the number is symbolic of what falls short of seven

debates.q: What kind of wisdom does the verse call for?

sides.view: Interpretive skill at an enigma, deliberately obscured to protect the writer
Moral rather than intellectual wisdom; treating it as a conundrum sacrifices the book’s dignity
A puzzle that has drawn all sorts of solutions and remains undecided

outliers.view: Reads the number forward rather than backward, as a coming age of culture and science so nearly perfect that faith is thought an impertinence
